correctness.rationale: The Apéry minimum is r+a(r+c(r)); positive residue wraps strictly increase cost. Adding a coin of value one and replacing any Mersenne coin b_i by two b_{i-1} when subtracting one prove the adjacent coin-cost changes by at most one; odd coins force differences exactly ±1. The resulting monotone residue thresholds have increments zero or two, and row-by-row terminal-gap counting proves the full maximal-run histogram, total and isolated-gap boundary. The standalone Dijkstra and direct gap-word script checks a=3..319 and all 25 s,n pairs through five, without serving as a substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 Gu–Li–Huang full text and the 2023 Liu–Xin–Ye–Yin full preprint establish related Apéry and global Frobenius/genus formulas for subfamilies and a dominating affine-repunit family. These are recognized as prior. Neither primary text states the multiplicity of every maximal *consecutive gap-run length* or its zero-or-two distribution, nor the sharp isolated-gap boundary for (2^s+1)2^n−1. Actual indexed searches also surfaced only distinct two-generator or plus-one Proth gap-run results. The new claim refines known numerical-set data and does not claim an original Apéry method; an implicit or unindexed exact specialization is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The earlier arXiv:2306.03459 may contain an unstated implication or variant that immediately yields the same histogram; its complete full text was not inspected.
A general published theorem on monotone Apéry semigroups might implicitly combine with coin-cost parity to give the paired-run law without explicitly stating it.
Indexed published-finding corpus result summaries do not substitute for full-text checks where direct coverage is plausible.

value.rationale: Maximal consecutive gap intervals are a natural local invariant of a numerical semigroup, not determined by its Frobenius number or genus alone. The theorem classifies the frequency of every possible run length across an infinite family, with a universal exact multiplicity-two phenomenon and sharp isolated-gap/perfectness phase transition on the naturally studied generalized-Thabit parameter subfamily. This is structural and reproducible, not merely isolated low-parameter computations.
